conclusion: dc:creator is an ordered array of creator names; creators may be people, organizations or services. No software-only value constraint follows.
pdf:Producer identifies the tool creating the PDF; the schema does not prescribe product-name spelling.
xmp:CreateDate records resource creation; filesystem timestamps need not agree.

The declaration namespace is http://pdfa.org/declarations/. Document claims are scoped to that PDF, not its children. declarations is an unordered array of structured declarations; conformsTo is required, claimData optional. Actual conformance requires separate evidence.
The conformsTo URI separates its path and fragment with #. The registry identifier is distinct from a hyperlink anchor used in EA-PDF explanatory text.
The ISO/TS 32005 registry identifier is https://pdfa.org/declarations#iso32005. claimBy and claimDate are recommended, other claim fields optional; they are not additional mandatory EA-PDF fields.

edition: April 2012; supporting dependency review, not certification of the cited 2019 ISO edition
conclusion: Sections 7.4-7.9 distinguish permitted XMP XML equivalents from general RDF forms. Section 8.2.2.3 treats GUID as a normal simple string with exact comparison, not a URI or a prescribed UUID format. Generic syntax validation remains upstream.

Agent includes people, groups and software. mbox relates an agent to a personal Internet mailbox, typically identified by a mailto URI; it does not impose the current helper SMTP-domain regular expression or prohibit additional FOAF fields.
All 26 open/closed reports and their comments reviewed; seven directly concern EA-PDF. Applicable findings are linked to rules and unresolved questions; proposals are not automatically adopted.

ISO-approved erratum 86 permits DPM name values with valid UTF-8 decoded bytes. This resolves the apparent type conflict raised by report-an-issue #13 without changing EA-PDF Table 8 names. Exact DPM decoding coverage remains a dependency audit item.

ISO-approved erratum 374 defines the MCAF array in a named property dictionary for AF marked-content sequences. The validator reads this representation as operational evidence for uncovered EA-PDF checks; it does not add a duplicate generic ISO/PDF-A conformance assertion.

Exact cited publication and relevant collection reference reviewed. EA-PDF independently mandates PDF 1.7 extension level 5 and prohibits Collection D; no broader inherited-standard or reader certification.
